title: Clio Completes Landmark $1B vLex Acquisition and Announces $500M Series G Funding Round at $5B Valuation
author: Clio

kp.k: Clio completed its $1 billion vLex acquisition
kp.d: The company press release reports completion of Clio’s US$1 billion acquisition of vLex and characterizes it as the largest M&A transaction ever in legal technology. It presents the transaction as accelerating Clio’s development into an AI-first company, while offering no independent evidence for the claimed historical ranking or expected effects.
qs: Clio, the global leader in legal AI technology, today announced it has completed its US$1 billion acquisition of vLex, one of the most significant transactions in legal technology history.
These milestones accelerate Clio's evolution as an AI-first company and reinforce its leadership in a new category of legal technology that connects the business and practice of law.

kp.k: New financing supports AI development and further acquisitions
kp.d: Clio reports closing a US$500 million Series G round led by NEA at a US$5 billion valuation, alongside a US$350 million debt facility led by Blackstone and funds managed by Blue Owl Capital. The company says this financing will support AI innovation, the vLex acquisition, and rapid pursuit of future strategic opportunities.
qs: The completion of the deal coincides with the closing of Clio's US$500 million Series G funding round, led by New Enterprise Associates (NEA), valuing the company at US$5 billion.

Clio's financing also includes a strategic US$350 million debt facility led by Blackstone (NYSE: BX) and funds managed by Blue Owl Capital (NYSE: OWL), two global leaders in private credit and technology lending.

This financing supports transformational moves like the acquisition of vLex and gives us the flexibility to act quickly on future opportunities that advance our mission and shape the future of legal technology.

kp.k: Clio combines legal operations with substantive legal intelligence
kp.d: The announced Intelligent Legal Work Platform combines Clio’s legal operating system and AI-enabled products with vLex’s Vincent AI and legal database. Clio claims this integration connects the operational mechanics and substantive practice of law in one environment, linking practice management, research, drafting, and firm operations.
qs: The close of the vLex acquisition unites Clio's legal operating system with vLex's Vincent AI, powered by one of the world's most comprehensive global legal databases.
Together, they form the Intelligent Legal Work Platform, connecting the business and practice of law through AI that understands both the mechanics and substance of legal work.

By combining practice management, research, drafting, and firm operations into connected AI-powered workflows, Clio empowers legal professionals to move from insight to action with greater speed and precision.

kp.k: Platform shifts from recording work to executing workflows
kp.d: Clio frames its platform strategy as a transition from a passive system of record to a “system of action.” It predicts that integrating AI across the legal-work lifecycle will convert static information into adaptive systems and improve the speed, precision, and value of legal workflows; these are company claims rather than reported comparative findings.
qs: Recently revealed at ClioCon 2025, this platform represents a shift from a traditional system of record to a system of action that leverages dynamic intelligence.

Through the integration of AI across the full lifecycle of legal work, Clio transforms static information into intelligent systems that continuously learn, adapt, and deliver increasing value over time.

kp.k: Vincent AI draws on extensive global legal data
kp.d: The release identifies vLex’s data holdings as the foundation for Vincent AI’s legal reasoning, specifying more than one billion editorially enriched documents across 110 jurisdictions. Clio claims that combining this resource with its own AI capabilities will improve accuracy, efficiency, and confidence, but provides no benchmark or evaluation results supporting those performance claims.
qs: Vincent AI provides the strongest foundation for legal reasoning, drawing from vLex's library of more than one billion editorially enriched documents across 110 jurisdictions.
Combined with Clio's AI capabilities across Clio Work, Clio Manage, Clio Grow, and Clio Draft, the platform delivers unparalleled accuracy, efficiency, and confidence in every task.

kp.k: Acquisitions extend Clio into enterprise legal services
kp.d: Clio says vLex will accelerate its expansion beyond small and midsize firms into large law firms and other global legal organizations. It links this strategy to its March 2025 acquisition of ShareDo, subsequently developed as Clio Operate for large firms and corporate legal departments, and to the creation of a dedicated Clio for Enterprise division.
qs: The integration of vLex also accelerates Clio's expansion into the enterprise market, extending its reach from small and midsize firms to the world's largest legal organizations.
This follows Clio's March 2025 acquisition of ShareDo, which has evolved into Clio Operate, an adaptive work management platform for large firms and corporate legal departments.
Together, vLex and Clio Operate anchor a new era of enterprise innovation through Clio for Enterprise, a division dedicated to serving the complex needs of global legal teams.

kp.k: Clio Operate targets complex global legal-team workflows
kp.d: The release describes Clio Operate as an enterprise work-management product combining configurable workflows, compliance, collaboration, analytics, and matter management. It is presented as serving both provider-side large law firms and buyer-side corporate legal departments, with existing use by leading UK firms and availability in the United States and other international markets.
qs: Clio Operate delivers configurability, compliance, and collaboration at scale.
It unifies workflows, analytics, and matter management across global teams, providing the structure large firms require with the flexibility individual lawyers need.
Already used by leading firms in the United Kingdom, Clio Operate is now available in the United States and other international markets.

kp.k: Enterprise offering promises trusted and court-admissible AI
kp.d: Clio asserts that combining its operational technology with vLex’s legal intelligence will connect performance data and decision-making through AI described as accurate, court-admissible, and grounded in trusted legal data. The release does not explain the applicable meaning, jurisdictional conditions, verification process, or evidence supporting “court-admissible.”
qs: The combination of Clio's operational technology with vLex's legal intelligence connects performance, data, and decision-making through AI that is accurate, court-admissible, and built on trusted legal data.

kp.k: The deal adds specialized legal and technical expertise
kp.d: Clio CEO Jack Newton says more than 350 experts in law, data, and technology will join Clio through the transaction. He predicts that combining these personnel and tools will create a legal intelligence platform with a generational influence on how legal work is performed.
qs: With vLex now part of Clio, and 350+ experts in law, data, and technology joining our team, we are combining the best minds and the best tools to build the world's most powerful legal intelligence platform, a platform that will define how legal work is done for generations to come.

kp.k: Clio targets firms of every size globally
kp.d: The release positions the combined company as bringing legal AI to organizations ranging from small firms to global enterprises. Clio reports that its existing products are trusted by hundreds of thousands of legal professionals in more than 130 countries and approved by over 100 bar associations and law societies, figures offered as indicators of reach rather than evidence of AI outcomes.
qs: The company is positioned to bring legal AI technology to firms of every size and extend its global reach with the most comprehensive platform in the industry

Trusted by hundreds of thousands of legal professionals in more than 130 countries, and approved by over 100 bar associations and law societies worldwide, Clio sets the standard for innovation and client success across the legal profession.

kp.k: Investors endorse Clio’s AI-led market strategy
kp.d: NEA Co-CEO Tony Florence attributes the investment to Clio’s performance, execution, financial strength, and AI strategy, claiming that AI integration is reshaping professional work. Oakley Capital’s acceptance of Clio equity for part of the vLex transaction is separately presented by Clio as confidence in the combination’s AI potential and global opportunity.
qs: The company has built one of the most trusted platforms in legal technology, and its integration of AI is reshaping how work is done across the profession.
We are proud to partner with Jack and his team through this exciting stage of growth and believe Clio's vision and financial strength position it to lead this industry for decades to come.

The transaction also includes a significant equity component, with Oakley Capital, a leading European private equity firm and majority shareholder in vLex, choosing to take Clio stock as part of the transaction.
They share our belief in the transformative potential of AI in the legal industry and the scale of opportunity ahead.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Clio claims that integrating legal intelligence with practice-management software turns legal technology from a repository of information into an AI-powered platform for executing connected legal workflows.
pts.d: The company press release says the combination of Clio's operating system and vLex's Vincent AI connects the business and substance of legal practice. It claims improvements in speed, precision, accuracy, efficiency and decision-making across research, drafting and firm operations, and says the integrated systems continuously learn and increase their value. These are Clio's descriptions of the platform's capabilities, rather than independently established performance findings.

pts.k: Clio claims its acquisitions broaden the market for integrated legal AI from small and midsize firms to large firms and corporate legal departments worldwide.
pts.d: The release presents vLex and Clio Operate, formerly ShareDo, as the foundations of its enterprise expansion. It claims the combined offering connects operational performance, legal data and decision-making, while supporting global workflow coordination, compliance and collaboration. Clio also characterizes the resulting AI as accurate and court-admissible, without specifying the scope or conditions of that characterization.

pts.k: Clio and its quoted executives and investor predict that the acquisition and financing will support further AI innovation and enduring influence over legal work.
pts.d: Clio presents the completed US$1 billion vLex acquisition, US$500 million Series G round at a US$5 billion valuation and US$350 million debt facility as resources for accelerating AI development and strategic acquisitions. CEO Jack Newton predicts that the combined legal intelligence platform will define legal work for generations. NEA Co-CEO Tony Florence says Clio's AI integration is already reshaping professional work and predicts decades of industry leadership. CFO Curt Sigfstead describes financing as enabling further strategic opportunities. These statements concern vendor expansion and anticipated industry influence, not measured changes in lawyer employment or legal-service prices.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The release supports its claims with database scale, product integration, reported adoption, transaction resources and executive or investor endorsements; it supplies no outcome benchmarks.
pts.d: Clio cites more than one billion editorially enriched documents spanning 110 jurisdictions as Vincent AI's legal-reasoning foundation, and more than 350 incoming experts as development capacity. It reports existing UK enterprise use, a user base across more than 130 countries and approval by over 100 bar associations and law societies. Financing and Oakley Capital's acceptance of Clio stock are presented as confidence in the strategy. The source provides no comparative accuracy tests, quantified time savings, client-outcome studies or judicial examples supporting its accuracy, efficiency or court-admissibility claims. Its adoption and approval figures concern the company or platform generally, not demonstrated effects of the newly integrated AI offering.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The release mixes present-tense capability claims at the 2025 acquisition closing with open-ended predictions of growing value and decades-long influence.
pts.d: The platform is described as recently revealed at ClioCon 2025, and the vLex acquisition and Series G financing as completed at publication. Enterprise expansion follows the March 2025 ShareDo acquisition, with Clio Operate described as already available beyond the UK. Claimed workflow benefits depend on combining vLex's legal intelligence with Clio's applications and integrating AI across legal work. Continuous improvement is projected 'over time,' while Newton and Florence use generational and decades-long horizons. No detailed integration timetable, quantified performance targets or conditions for court admissibility are supplied.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The claimed beneficiaries are legal professionals, firms of all sizes and corporate legal departments, with indirect benefits asserted for their clients.
pts.d: For individual legal professionals, Clio claims faster, more precise research, drafting and operational work. For small and midsize firms, the offering extends an existing practice-management platform into integrated legal AI. For large firms and corporate legal departments, it promises configurable workflows, analytics, matter management and coordination across global teams. Clio is the software provider expanding its enterprise and international market presence. Clients worldwide are named as eventual beneficiaries, but the release does not specify changes in fees, access to justice, staffing, employment or human verification requirements.
